statement: You receive one line holding an infix expression of single-letter operands, the operators + - * / ^ and round brackets. Print its postfix form. Stream operands straight to the output. Hold operators on a stack: before pushing one, pop to the output every stacked operator of higher precedence, or equal precedence when the arrival is left-associative (^ is right-associative). Push ( always; on ) pop to the output until the matching ( is removed. At the end, flush the stack.

example.why: Inside the brackets c^d yields cd^ and the subtraction gives cd^e-; the * then binds before the +.

hint: One comparison rules the stack: pop while the top binds at least as tightly, then push.
mistake: Popping equal-precedence operators for ^ too - right-associativity means a^b^c groups from the right.
